records.name: Tokyo Dome
records.description: An indoor stadium in Bunkyo's Koraku district, opened in 1988 as the home of the Yomiuri Giants baseball team. Its air-supported roof earned it the nickname "The Big Egg."

photo.credit: Edoson no Tokuzo (江戸村のとくぞう)

records.name: Tokyo Dome City Attractions
records.description: An amusement park in the Tokyo Dome City complex, opened in 1958 as Korakuen Amusement Park and renamed in 2003. Rides include the Thunder Dolphin roller coaster and the Big O Ferris wheel.

records.name: Koishikawa Korakuen
records.description: A large Edo-period daimyo garden established in 1629 by Tokugawa Yorifusa and expanded by his son Tokugawa Mitsukuni. One of the few surviving daimyo gardens, designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty and Special Historic Site in 1952.

records.name: Rikugien
records.description: A metropolitan Japanese garden built between 1695 and 1702 for daimyo Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu, later restored by the Iwasaki family and donated to Tokyo in 1938. Designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty in 1953.

tips.text: General admission is 300 yen (150 yen for age 65+); free for Tokyo junior high students and younger.
Hours are 9am-5pm, extended to 9pm during spring and autumn illumination periods.

records.hours: 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (extended to 9:00 PM during spring/autumn illuminations)
records.station: Komagome Station (JR Yamanote Line / Tokyo Metro Namboku Line)

records.name: Koishikawa Botanical Garden
records.description: A botanical garden and arboretum operated by the University of Tokyo Graduate School of Science, spanning about 16 hectares with roughly 4,000 plant species. Designated a National Historic Site and Place of Scenic Beauty in 2012.

tips.text: Open daily except Mondays; an admission fee is required.

records.name: Chinzanso Garden
records.description: A Japanese garden established in 1877 on the former hillside home of Meiji-era statesman Yamagata Aritomo, now part of the Hotel Chinzanso Tokyo property. Features a centuries-old three-story pagoda relocated from Hiroshima, a waterfall, and stone lanterns.

records.name: Higo Hosokawa Garden
records.description: A circular hill-and-pond garden that was formerly the residence of the Hosokawa family, daimyo of the Kumamoto domain. The current garden was created in 1961 and renamed from Shin-Edogawa Garden in 2017. A gate connects it to the neighboring Eisei Bunko Museum.

tips.text: Open 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM; admission is free.

records.station: Edogawabashi Station / Waseda Station (Toden Arakawa Line)

records.name: Akamon (Red Gate), University of Tokyo
records.description: A red-lacquered gate built in 1827 to welcome a Tokugawa shogun's daughter as bride to the Maeda clan lord. It survived fires, earthquakes and wartime bombing and is now a designated Important Cultural Property and symbol of the University of Tokyo.

records.name: Yasuda Auditorium, University of Tokyo
records.description: An Art Deco-influenced Gothic auditorium completed in 1925 with a donation from businessman Yasuda Zenjiro, designed by architects Yoshikazu Uchida and Hideto Kishida as part of the campus's post-earthquake reconstruction. It is the University of Tokyo's central symbolic building.

records.name: Sanshiro Pond
records.description: A pond within the University of Tokyo's Hongo campus, formally named Ikutokuen Shinji-ike, built in 1638 as part of a Maeda clan daimyo garden. It takes its popular name from Natsume Soseki's novel Sanshiro, in which the protagonist meets the heroine here.
records.address: University of Tokyo Hongo Campus, Bunkyo, Tokyo

records.name: Yushima Tenmangu Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine, commonly called Yushima Tenjin, first established in 458 and expanded in 1355 to enshrine the scholarship deity Tenjin. It is popular with students praying for exam success and is known for its plum blossoms.

tips.text: The Ume Matsuri (plum blossom festival) runs from February 7 to March 7 each year.

records.station: Yushima Station (Chiyoda Line), 2-minute walk from Exit 3

records.name: Yushima Seido
records.description: A Confucian temple founded in 1632 and moved to its current site in 1691, once home to the shogunate's Shoheiko academy. The present hall, designed by Ito Chuta, was completed in 1935 after the original was destroyed in the 1923 earthquake, and the grounds hold a large statue of Confucius.

records.name: Nezu Shrine
records.description: A Shinto shrine relocated to its current Nezu site in 1705 by shogun Tokugawa Tsunayoshi, one of the oldest places of worship in Tokyo. It is known for a hillside path of vermilion torii gates and its spring Tsutsuji Matsuri (azalea festival).

tips.text: The Tsutsuji Matsuri (azalea festival) runs from early April through early May.

records.station: Nezu Station (Chiyoda Line), 5-minute walk; also Sendagi Station and Todaimae Station

records.name: Hakusan Jinja
records.description: A Shinto shrine established in 948, moved to its present location in 1655. It hosts the Bunkyo Hydrangea Festival each June, when roughly 3,000 hydrangeas bloom across the shrine grounds and adjoining Hakusan Park.

tips.text: The Bunkyo Ajisai (Hydrangea) Festival is held annually in mid-June.

records.name: Gokokuji
records.description: A Shingon Buddhist temple built in 1681 by fifth shogun Tokugawa Tsunayoshi in dedication to his mother. It is one of the few historic Tokyo sites to survive World War II air raids intact, and its main hall and Gekkoden pavilion are Important Cultural Properties.

records.name: Denzuin
records.description: A Pure Land Buddhist temple founded in 1415, renamed Denzuin after Tokugawa Ieyasu buried his mother Odai no Kata here in 1602. Stone tombs of several Tokugawa family women remain on the grounds, though wartime bombing destroyed the prewar temple buildings.

records.name: Bunkyo Civic Center Observation Deck
records.description: A free public observation deck on the 25th floor of the Bunkyo ward office building, completed in 1994, standing about 105 meters above ground with a 330-degree view of Tokyo including Mount Fuji, Mount Tsukuba, and the Tokyo Skytree on clear days.

tips.text: Entry to the observation lounge is free.

records.name: Bunkyo Museum
records.description: The local history museum for Bunkyo ward, opened in April 1991, with permanent exhibits spanning prehistoric to modern times and a particular focus on the 1884 discovery of Yayoi-period pottery in the ward.

tips.text: Admission is 100 yen for adults; free for junior high school age and younger.

records.hours: 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM, closed Mondays (or Tuesday if Monday is a national holiday)
records.station: Hongo-sanchome Station (Marunouchi/Oedo Line); also near Kasuga Station

records.name: Yayoi Museum
records.description: An art museum in the Yayoi district displaying illustration and print work from the Meiji, Taisho, and Showa eras, situated next to the Takehisa Yumeji Museum.

tips.text: Closed Mondays, during exhibit changeovers, and year-end/New Year holidays; last entry 30 minutes before closing.

records.name: Takehisa Yumeji Museum
records.description: A museum dedicated to Taisho-era painter Takehisa Yumeji (1884-1934), known for his bijin-ga (paintings of beautiful women), holding over 3,000 of his works with quarterly rotating exhibitions.

tips.text: About a 17-minute walk from Nezu Station, Exit 1.

records.station: Nezu Station (Chiyoda Line), Exit 1, about 17-minute walk

records.name: Mori Ogai Memorial Museum
records.description: A museum built in 2012 on the site of Kancho-ro, the Sendagi residence where novelist, critic, and military surgeon Mori Ogai lived for 30 years, displaying artifacts and manuscripts from his career.

tips.text: Closed the fourth Monday and Tuesday of each month (except holidays) and year-end/New Year holidays.

records.hours: 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM daily (last entry 30 min before closing)
records.station: Sendagi Station (Chiyoda Line), Exit 1, about 15-minute walk

records.name: Tokyo Waterworks Historical Museum
records.description: A museum established in 1995 documenting 400 years of Tokyo's water supply history, from Edo-period wooden aqueducts to the modern system, with English audio guides available. The Kanda Aqueduct Stone Pipe remains stand at the adjoining Hongo Water Supply Park.

tips.text: Admission is free; English audio guides are available at no charge.

records.station: Suidobashi Station (Toei Mita Line) or Hongo-sanchome Station (Toei Oedo Line), each about 8-minute walk

records.name: Yayoi 2-chome Site
records.description: An archaeological site marking where a distinctive red-clay jar was unearthed in 1884, giving its name to Japan's Yayoi period and Yayoi pottery style. Designated a National Historic Site in 1976; the original jar is held at the University of Tokyo's museum as a National Important Cultural Property.

tips.text: Public access with no facilities; about a 3-minute walk from Nezu Station.

records.name: Ushi-Tenjin Kitano Shrine
records.description: A small Shinto shrine founded in 1184 after Minamoto no Yoritomo reported a dream of the scholarship deity Sugawara no Michizane seated on a bull. Counted among the Seven Edo Tenjin shrines, it moved to its present Kasuga-area site during the 1624-1645 Kan'ei era.

records.name: Higuchi Ichiyo Former Residence Site (Kikuzaka)
records.description: A marked site in the Kikuzaka area of Hongo where novelist Higuchi Ichiyo lived with her family, one of several spots in the neighborhood connected to the writer, who spent about ten years of her short life in the area.

records.name: Basho-an (Sekiguchi Basho Hermitage)
records.description: A reconstructed hut marking where haiku poet Matsuo Basho lived from 1677 to 1680 while working on the Kanda aqueduct in the Sekiguchi district, beside the Kanda River. The small garden includes banana trees, Basho's namesake plant, and a pond.
records.station: Edogawabashi Station, under 10-minute walk along the Kanda River

records.name: Edogawa Park
records.description: A narrow riverside park along the Kanda River that has been a hanami (cherry blossom viewing) spot since the late Edo period, with around 200 cherry trees and over 2,000 azaleas lining the banks.

tips.text: Cherry blossoms typically bloom late March to early April, with evening illumination from 5:30 PM to 9:00 PM during the season.

records.name: Toyo Bunko Museum
records.description: Japan's largest library devoted to Asian studies, founded in 1924 by Mitsubishi's Iwasaki Hisaya around a purchased China-studies collection. Its public museum wing displays rare manuscripts and historical maps from the library's roughly 950,000-volume holdings.

tips.text: Closed every Tuesday (open on the holiday and closed the following Wednesday if Tuesday is a national holiday); last admission 30 minutes before closing.

records.station: Komagome Station, Exit 2 (JR Yamanote Line / Tokyo Metro Namboku Line), 8-minute walk

records.name: Eisei Bunko Museum
records.description: A private museum holding art and historical documents preserved over generations by the Hosokawa family, daimyo of Higo (present-day Kumamoto). Turned into a foundation in 1950, the public museum opened in 1973 and holds eight National Treasures among roughly 112,000 items.
